answer: Split each epoch's fixed reward pool pro-rata across registered identities and charge a burned fee B at every registration. One more clone adds only its marginal dilution of that pool, at most a single identity's share, while costing B. The mechanism is safe while B exceeds a clone's lifetime marginal share: a mirror of clone keys, each a faint echo of one operator, pays the copper toll again and wins no new slice. Enforcement is plain ledger arithmetic. Assumption: the per-epoch pool is truly fixed. Limit: when honest membership is thin, each share is large, so B must sit painfully high.
